SELECTED_INDEX: 8
CONFIDENCE: 0.36
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic pattern of a para-disubstituted benzene: very strong ring-breathing at 999 cm⁻¹, a strong C–H out-of-plane band at 818 cm⁻¹, and paired ring C=C stretches at 1602/1589 cm⁻¹.  The pronounced band at 619 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of an aromatic C–Cl stretch, while the moderate bands at 1028 and 1247 cm⁻¹ match the C–O stretching modes of a benzylic –CH₂OH group.  Weak CH stretches at 2938–2879 cm⁻¹ and a CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1458 cm⁻¹ are consistent with the single benzylic –CH₂– moiety.  Among the candidates only OCc1ccc(Cl)cc1 (p-chlorobenzyl alcohol, index 8) possesses exactly this combination of (i) para-disubstituted ring, (ii) an aromatic C–Cl bond, and (iii) a benzylic alcohol C–O bond, matching the key Raman features, whereas candidates lacking either the para pattern, the aryl-Cl band, or the benzylic C–O group fit less well.
